hypothesis: Question: recorded rentals grew strongly from 2011 to early 2012 (train mean 154 vs last-60-day mean 232 in idea-f87923 findings). Which representation of that level shift transfers into May-June 2012? Prior evidence: idea-baseline-2 (squared-error HGB, all features incl. elapsed_day and yr, dev RMSE 59.99, group MAE 40.95) is the best valid measurement; idea-f87923's detached additive log1p level offset (const60=+0.55, i.e. ~1.74x on a shape model trained without yr/elapsed_day) selected by a 2-fold internal comparison overshot badly on dev (pred_mean 334, RMSE 93.3), and its two internal folds disagreed on the sign of the raw baseline's bias (-45 vs +8). This changed my view: bolting a separately estimated level onto a shape model plus small-fold selection is fragile; the level should be learned jointly with the covariates, and internal folds should serve as diagnostics, not as the selector. Proposal: hold every baseline-2 hyperparameter fixed (max_iter=250, lr=0.08, max_leaf_nodes=31, l2=1, random_state=1729, default early_stopping='auto', which with >10000 rows is likely active; n_iter_ is reported) and change only loss='poisson', submitting that model with all features. Contrasting expectations: (A) if rentals scale multiplicatively (hour/weather shape x growth level), the Poisson link lets the same trees represent the yr/elapsed_day effect as a ratio and dev RMSE falls below 59.99 with reduced |bias| on the recorded holdouts; (B) if dev error is dominated by high-count hourly noise, Poisson deviance down-weights large-count errors and dev RMSE is equal or worse (an informative negative for the multiplicative-transfer view). Diagnostics only (no selection): three chronological 30-day holdouts (cuts at last-90/-60/-30 train days) comparing squared_all, poisson_all and poisson without elapsed_day, reporting RMSE/MAE/bias/pred_mean per fold, plus the Jan-Apr 2012/2011 mean ratio to expose the raw growth factor. Any fit failure falls back to squared_error and is reported in findings. One city and one 61-day period cannot establish general benefit.
